goal: Move the unlocked-session signing-key cache in apps/extension/src/handlers/key-session.ts off a plain in-memory Map, which Chrome can silently empty by idle-killing and restarting the MV3 service worker independent of the user's chosen auto-lock timeout, onto chrome.storage.session, which survives that restart the same way Session.unlockedWalletIds already does.
outcome: key-session.ts's store (cacheKey, getCachedKey, hasCachedKey, removeCachedKey, clearKeyCache) is backed by chrome.storage.session instead of a module-level Map, with an async signature; wallet-lifecycle.ts, transfer.ts, upload.ts, and approval.ts (its only callers) await the new async calls. A wallet that chrome.storage.session and the auto-lock timeout both still consider unlocked never throws "Wallet is locked" merely because the service worker restarted; it only locks when the user's auto-lock timeout elapses or they explicitly lock.

requirements.statement: No in-memory fallback path: chrome.storage.session is the only store for cached signing keys; no legacy Map remains alongside it.
Key material is never written to chrome.storage.local or any disk-backed store -- chrome.storage.session only, matching Session.unlockedWalletIds's existing guarantee.

Simulating a service-worker restart (clearing module state without clearing chrome.storage.session) leaves a previously unlocked wallet's cached key readable and signing calls succeed without a re-prompt.
clearKeyCache() and the auto-lock-expiry path both still remove all cached keys from chrome.storage.session, so an expired or explicitly locked session can never be used to sign.
deleteWallet still removes only that wallet's cached key, not the whole session store.
